 Georgia jumps to the top of Week 11 Coaches Poll
 Jake Rowe @ JakeMRowe 50m 0 Share Share 
 Georgia is the nation’s No. 1 team in the US LBM Coaches Poll . The Bulldogs also have a strong chance of landing No. 1 in the AP poll, released later today, and the College Football Playoff Rankings, which come out on Wednesday.
 Utah is No. 2 after dispatching of BYU. Notre Dame rises to No. 3, with UCLA at No. 4, Indiana at No. 5 and Miami at No. 6. Alabama, Texas, Tennessee and Texas Tech, in that order, round out the top 10. 
 The change at the top is due Miami’s loss at Notre Dame coupled with a dominant UGA win over Ole Miss. Georgia hammered Ole Miss 42-7 in Oxford, handing Kirby Smart his first win in three tries at Vaught Hemingway Stadium. The Bulldogs led the game 28-0 at halftime, and led 35-0 at one point.
 Ole Miss, led by Trinidad Chambliss, turned the ball over twice and didn’t reach the end zone until the fourth quarter. Georgia’s defense held the Rebels to 2.1 yards per carry and just 3.7 yards per play. The Bulldogs also recorded five sacks against Chambliss after sacking him zero times in the two games against him in 2025.
 Offensively, Georgia was explosive and efficient. Prior to three kneel downs to end the game, which also ruined a perfect day for the Bulldogs in the red zone, UGA was averaging over eight yards per play. It was four of four at getting touchdowns in the red zone, too. Georgia had nine runs of 10 yards or more and four of 15 yards or more. The Bulldogs also produced three pass plays of 20 yards or more and three scrimmage plays of 40 yards or more.
 Gunner Stockton finished with four touchdowns through the air and another on the ground, giving him 13 scores in three career games against the Rebels. 
 Ole Miss fell to No. 17 with the loss. 
 Next up for the Bulldogs is a clash with Missouri, now unranked in the Coaches Poll, at Sanford Stadium. It’ll be Georgia’s first home game since its loss to Auburn last month. That game is set for 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC.
